Indeed, by definition of a pp-interpretation, the preimage bar E of E is pp-definable in mathbb A, and therefore preserved by Pol(mathbb A). A pseudo-loop in bar E yields a pseudo-loop in E modulo Aut(Q). Moreover, bar E is smooth and has pseudo-algebraic length modulo Aut(Q). By Creftheorem:tractable_pols, mathbb A is preserved by one of ellell, min, mi, mx, their duals, or a constant operation. Accordingly, mathbb G is preserved by one of these operations, and thus by all operations in its generated clone. Clearly, every non-empty relation preserved by a constant operation contains even a loop. Moreover, mathbb G contains a pseudo-loop if and only if -mathbb G does. Recalling that, for fin\ellell,min,mi,mx\, mathbb G is preserved by gendual(f) if and only if -mathbb G is preserved by genf, this allows us to restrict ourselves to the cases where mathbb G is preserved by one of genellell, genmin, genmi, and genmx. In the first case, let S subseteq E be smooth, weakly connected, and of pseudo-algebraic length~1 modulo Aut(Q). By Creflemma:ll:inductionstep, genrelS'ellellsubseteq E contains a pseudo-loop modulo Aut(Q). In all the other cases, we can directly apply Creflemma:pp:inductionstep, yielding a pseudo-loop modulo Aut(Q) within E.

nodes.statement: Suppose that there is ainpr_1(E) having two outgoing edges of different splits, i.e.\;ensuremathsxspace(binomab)neqensuremathsxspace(binomac). It is easy to see by a case analysis that then, ensuremathsxspace(ensuremathtxxspace(binomab,binomac)) is half-constant. An analogous argument can also be made whenever some ainpr_1(E) has two incoming edges of different splits. It remains to consider the case where for all ainpr_1(E), all outgoing edges share the same, non-half-constant split, and the same is true for all incoming edges. By our assumptions, there is Ssubseteq E that is smooth, weakly connected and of pseudo-algebraic length~1. This implies that for some minmathbb N, S is m-linked. Now, note that in any m-fence and any upper tip a^ell,m of this fence, both its incoming edges must share the same split. In particular, a^ell,m-1 and a^ell+1,m-1 must share the same split with respect to a uniform partition. By a slight generalization of the argument at the beginning of this proof, also a^ell,m-2 and a^ell+1,m-2 must share the same split with respect to a uniform partition: Were this not the case, ensuremathsxspace(ensuremathtxxspace(binoma^ell,m-1a^ell,m-2,binoma^ell+1,m-1a^ell,m-2)) would be constant in the top half. This argument can be repeated inductively to show that the two lower tips a^ell,0 and a^ell+1,0 share the same split with respect to a uniform partition. Now, comparing their outgoing edges within the fence, and repeating the argument, now for outgoing instead of incoming edges, and continuing this argument, flipping whenever we arrive at the tips, we ultimately arrive at the conclusion that all lower tips of the fence must share the same split with respect to a uniform partition. Due to m-linkedness and omega-categoricity, there is an m-fence in S that contains orbit-representants of all vertices in pr_1(S) as lower tips. This implies that all tuples in pr_1(S) share the same split. Since we assumed that there are no half-constant split edges, S contains only uniformly split edges.

As in the proof of \Cref{temp:theorem:pseudoloop}, we may without loss of generality assume that $\mathbb G$ is a digraph defined on $A^k$ whose edge relation $E^{\mathbb A}$ is preserved by $\mathrm{Pol}(\mathbb A)$. 
   
   
   
   By \Cref{phylo:theorem:classification}, we are in one of two cases. If $\mathbb A$ has a constant endomorphism, then the statement is trivial.
   
   It thus remains to prove the statement for the case that $\ensuremath{\mathrm{tx}}\xspace\in\mathrm{Pol}(\mathbb A)$.
   
   
   
   

   

   
   
    
    
    
    
    
    

   

    
    
    
    
    The proof is by induction on $k$. 
    
    For $k=1$, every edge is a pseudo-loop.
    
    Now, suppose that we have already proven the statement for all $\ell<k$ for some $k$.
    
    By \Cref{phylo:lemma:graph:fence}, $E$ either contains a uniformly split or a half-constant split edge. 
    
    Suppose that the former applies, and let $\binom{a}{b}\in E$ be uniformly split.
    
    Then there also is a uniformly split edge in $E'$, so without loss of generality, let $\binom{a}{b}\in E'$.
    
    \mo{Denote the set of entries of $\binom{a}{b}$ by $U$.
    
    By our induction hypothesis, the relation $\mathrm{pr}_{I_0(a)}(E)$ contains a pseudo-loop $\binom{\tilde c}{\tilde d}$. 
    
    Let $\binom{c}{d}\in\mathrm{pr}_{I_0(a)}^{-1}(\binom{\tilde c}{\tilde d})$, denote the set of entries of $\binom{c}{d}$ by $V$, and choose $\alpha\in\mathrm{Aut}\Phylo$ such that 
    
    \[
        \alpha V\prec U \textnormal{ as well as } \alpha V|U.
    \]
    
    
    Consequently, by $\ensuremath{\mathrm{tx}}\xspace$ being an affine tree operation, we get that, for $\binom{a'}{b'}\mathrel{\mathop:}\mathrel{\mkern-1.2mu}=\ensuremath{\mathrm{tx}}\xspace(\binom{a}{b},\binom{\alpha c}{\alpha d}),$
    \[
    \ensuremath{\mathrm{s}}\xspace\binom{a'}{b'}=\ensuremath{\mathrm{s}}\xspace\binom{a}{b}  \textnormal{, and }\binom{\mathrm{pr}_{I_0(a)}a'}{\mathrm{pr}_{I_0(a)}b'}\sim\binom{\tilde c}{\tilde d}.
    \]
    In other words, $\binom{a'}{b'}$ splits (uniformly) just like $\binom{a}{b}$, and the ``left" parts of both vertices, i.e.\;the parts assigned $0$ by $\ensuremath{\mathrm{s}}\xspace$, are in the same orbit.
    
    It thus remains to align the ``right" parts of the tuples.
    
    Again, we can exploit $\ensuremath{\mathrm{tx}}\xspace$ being an affine tree operation.
    
    Denote the set of entries of $\binom{a'}{b'}$ by $U'$.
    
    By the induction hypothesis, also $\mathrm{pr}_{I_1(a)}(E)$ contains a pseudoloop $\binom{\tilde e}{\tilde f}$. 
    
    Let $\binom{e}{f}\in\mathrm{pr}_{I_1(a)}^{-1}(\binom{\tilde e}{\tilde f})$, denote its set of entries by $W$, and choose $\beta\in\mathrm{Aut}(\Phylo)$ such that 
    
    \[
        U'_0\prec \beta W\prec U'_1 \textnormal{ as well as } U'_0| \beta W \textnormal{ and } U'_0\cup\beta W|U'_1.
    \]
    
    Similarly to the previous step, it follows for $\binom{a''}{b''}\mathrel{\mathop:}\mathrel{\mkern-1.2mu}=\ensuremath{\mathrm{tx}}\xspace(\binom{a'}{b'},\binom{\alpha c}{\alpha d})$ that
    \[
    \ensuremath{\mathrm{s}}\xspace\binom{a''}{b''}=\ensuremath{\mathrm{s}}\xspace\binom{a}{b}\textnormal{ and } \binom{\mathrm{pr}_{I_0(a)} a''}{\mathrm{pr}_{I_0(a)} b''}\sim\binom{\tilde c}{\tilde d}\textnormal{, while }
    \binom{\mathrm{pr}_{I_1(a)} a''}{\mathrm{pr}_{I_1(a)} b''}\sim\binom{\tilde e}{\tilde f}.
    \]
    As $\binom{a''}{b''}$ splits uniformly and both the ``left" and the ``right" parts of $a''$ and $b''$ are in the same orbits, we have $a''\sim b''$.
    }

    It remains to consider the case where $E$ contains no uniformly split edges, but a half-constant split edge. 
    
    \Cref{phylo:lemma:graph:even} yields an edge $\binom{e}{f}\in E$ whose entries $e$ and $f$ are algined to the $1$-st degree. 
    
    \Cref{phylo:prop:graph:pL} then yields a pseudo-loop.
    }

Take any $t\in \ensuremath{R}\xspace$, and consider its cyclic permutations $t=t^1,\ldots,t^n$. 
    
    Denote the set of entries of $t$ by $U$, and consider a sufficiently large finite set $V\supseteq U$ whose generic partition $(V_0,V_1)$ extends that of $U$.
    
    Then, there is an affine tree operation $\ensuremath{\mathrm{tx}}\xspace$ such that $\ensuremath{\mathrm{tx}}\xspace$ is dominated by $V_0$ over $V_1$, 
    $V_0\prec\ensuremath{\mathrm{tx}}\xspace(V_0\times V_1\cup V_1\times V_0)$,
    $\ensuremath{\mathrm{tx}}\xspace(V_0\times V_0\cup V_1\times V_1)\prec V_1$,
    and such that, for all $2\leq\ell\leq n$, $\nested{\ensuremath{\mathrm{tx}}\xspace}{\ell}(t^{n-\ell+1},\ldots,t^n)$ lies again within $V$.
    
    It follows from the properties of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{tx}}\xspace$ as an affine tree operation that the split of $t'\mathrel{\mathop:}\mathrel{\mkern-1.2mu}=\nested{\ensuremath{\mathrm{tx}}\xspace}{n}(t^1,\ldots,t^n)$ with respect to the partition $(V_0,V_1)$\footnote{Here, we do not use the standard split vector we defined, but the $\{0,1\}^{nk}$-tuple that assigns $0$ to entries lying in $V_0$, and $1$ to those in $V_1$.} is exactly $\sum \ensuremath{\mathrm{s}}\xspace(t^i)$, which is $k$-periodic. 
    
    If it is non-constant, this means that all vertices of $t'$ split uniformly.
    
    Otherwise, it means that $\sum_{1\leq i\leq n}\mathrm{pr}_i(\ensuremath{\mathrm{s}}\xspace(t))\in\{\overline 0,\overline 1\}$.
    
    Since this holds for any $t$, the claim is proven.

    By \Cref{phylo:lemma:hyp:parity,phylo:lemma:hyp:symmetric} applied to $\ensuremath{R}\xspace'$, the relation contains one of the following: 
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item\label{phylo:prop:hyp:pseudoloop:proof:en1:item1} A uniformly split tuple $t$,
        \item\label{phylo:prop:hyp:pseudoloop:proof:en1:item2} a tuple $t$ where $n-1$ vertices split uniformly, while the $n$-th splits constant with respect to the uniform partition, or 
        \item\label{phylo:prop:hyp:pseudoloop:proof:en1:item3} a tuple $t$ where $n-1$ vertices split uniformly, while the $n$-th splits dually with respect to the uniform partition. 
    \end{enumerate}
    
    In the first case, we can repeat the same argument as in the proof of \Cref{phylo:theorem:graph:pseudoloop} for uniformly split edges to generate pseudoloops via induction.
    
    In the second case, without loss of generality the constant split is $0^k$ and in the first position.
    
    Also in this case, we can utilise induction in a similar way:
    By the same induction hypothesis as in Case \ref{phylo:prop:hyp:pseudoloop:proof:en1:item1}, $\mathrm{pr}_{I_0(t_2)}(\ensuremath{R}\xspace)$ contains a pseudo-loop $\tilde u$.
    
    Taking $u\in\mathrm{pr}_{I_0(t_2)}^{-1}(\tilde u)$ now allows us to generate a tuple $t'$ in $\ensuremath{R}\xspace'$ with the same split as $t$ such that $\mathrm{pr}_{I_0(t_2)}(t')$ is a pseudo-loop. 
    
    
    Denote the set of entries of $t$ and $u$ by $U(t)$ and $U(u)$, respectively. Now, choose $\alpha\in\mathrm{Aut}\Phylo$ such that $U_0(t)\prec \alpha U(u)\prec U_1(t)$, $U_0(t)|\alpha U(u)$, and $U_0(t)\cup\alpha U(u)|U_1(t)$. 
    
    The hyperedge $t'\mathrel{\mathop:}\mathrel{\mkern-1.2mu}=\ensuremath{\mathrm{tx}}\xspace(t,\alpha u)$ now has the desired properties. 
    
    We now turn to synchronise the remaining halves of each subtuple of $t'$. 
    
    Here, we utilise the different split behaviour of $t'_1$ compared to the other subtuples. 
    
    Denote the set of entries of $t'$ by $U(t')$. 
    
    
    Choose $\beta\in\mathrm{Aut}\Phylo$ such that $U_0(t')\prec\beta U(t')\prec U_1(t')$, $U_0(t')|\beta U(t')$, $U_0(t')\cup \beta U(t')| U_1(t')$, and such that $\ensuremath{\mathrm{tx}}\xspace$ is dominated by $U_0$ over $\beta U$ over $U_1$.

    \begin{enumerate}
        \item\label{phylo:prop:hyp:pseudoloop:proof:en2:item1} $\ensuremath{\mathrm{s}}\xspace(t'')=\ensuremath{\mathrm{s}}\xspace(t')=\ensuremath{\mathrm{s}}\xspace(t)$, i.e., the split is unchanged,

    \end{enumerate}

    The only thing missing for $t^{(n)}$ to be a pseudo-loop is that in the constant-split tuple $t^{(n)}_1$, $\ensuremath{\mathrm{s}}\xspace(t^{(n)}_1)$ is not necessarily equal to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{s}}\xspace(t^{(n)}_2)$, meaning that the $I_0(t_2)$- and $I_1(t_2)$-part are not separated. 
    
    We achive this by once more cyclically shifting $t^{(n)}$, denoted by $u^{(n)}$ and setting $t^*\mathrel{\mathop:}\mathrel{\mkern-1.2mu}= \ensuremath{\mathrm{tx}}\xspace(t^{(n)},u^{(n)})$. 
    
    By the nature of $\ensuremath{\mathrm{tx}}\xspace$ as an affine tree operation, the split of $u^{(n)}_1$ is transferred to $t^*_1$, and we end up with a pseudo-loop.

    It remains to identify a pseudo-loop in Case \ref{phylo:prop:hyp:pseudoloop:proof:en1:item3}.
    
    Without loss of generality, all but the first vertex of $t$ split uniformly. 
    
    Very similarly to the previous cases, we can align all but the first vertex to be in the same orbit in a new tuple $t'\in\ensuremath{R}\xspace'$, while preserving $\ensuremath{\mathrm{s}}\xspace(t')=\ensuremath{\mathrm{s}}\xspace(t)$. 
    
    Denote the cyclic shift of $t'$ by $u'$ and consider $t''\mathrel{\mathop:}\mathrel{\mkern-1.2mu}= \ensuremath{\mathrm{tx}}\xspace(t',u')$. 
    
    Its split $\ensuremath{\mathrm{s}}\xspace(t'')$ assigns constant $1$ to all entries of the first two vertices, and constant $0$ to those of the remaining $n-2$ many. 
    
    Note that all vertices assigned constant $0$ are in the same orbit. 
    
    This strict split between the vertices now allows us to create a new hyperedge $t^{(3)}\in\ensuremath{R}\xspace'$, once more by utilising the affine tree operation $\ensuremath{\mathrm{tx}}\xspace$, where all vertices lie in the same orbit, namely that of those vertices of $t''$ assigned $0$.

If $R'$ 
    contains a tuple $t$ with $|M(t)|=1$, this tuple is min-clean.
    If $R'$ (which is non-empty by \Cref{lemma:derivative}) does not contain such a tuple, then by \Cref{l:minready} all tuples in $R'$ satisfy $|M(t)|= n$ and are, in particular, min-ready. 
    Take $t\in R'$ arbitrarily. 
    
    As in the proof of  \Cref{l:hypmi:minclean}, employing \Cref{l:int1hyp} instead of \Cref{l:mihypint},  one shows that   $\bigcap_{i \leq n}\mathrm{minx}(t_i)\neq \varnothing.$  
    Let $t^1, \dots, t^{n}$ denote all cyclic permutations of the tuple $t$. We have $t^i \in R'$ for all $i \leq n$ by cyclicity of $R$ and \Cref{lemma:derivative}.  The tuple   $s\mathrel{\mathop:}\mathrel{\mkern-1.2mu}=\nested{\mathrm{lex}}{n}(t^1, \dots, t^n)$ is contained in $R'$. Moreover, observe that $\min(s)=\nested{\mathrm{lex}}{m}(\min(t), \dots, \min(t))$ and $\mathrm{minx}(s_i)=\bigcap_{j\leq n}\mathrm{minx}(t_j)$ for all $i\leq n$. In particular, $s\in R'$ is  min-clean.
